extracted.intended_audience: prospective applicants and stakeholders in EU research and innovation (universities, research organisations, SMEs, industry, public authorities)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for organisations and consortia seeking Horizon Europe research & innovation funding, covering programme structure, eligibility, strategic alignment, missions, partnerships, and application procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal entities from the EU and associated countries can participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your organisation is a legal entity located in an EU Member State or an associated country. For participation rules and specific eligibility details, consult the Funding & Tenders portal and the 'Participation in Horizon Europe' documentation; contact the research enquiry service for questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application portal and procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All funding information and procedures on the Funding and Tenders portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit applications and follow call-specific instructions via the Funding & Tenders portal ('Apply now'). Use portal documents, model grant agreements and guides for specific actions. Attend info days and use the research enquiry service for procedural help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work programmes follow the Strategic Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of work programmes for Horizon Europe is prepared by strategic planning and the resultant strategic plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding opportunities under Horizon Europe are set out in work programmes — applicants must align proposals to topics and priorities as defined in the work programmes produced from the Strategic Plan. Download and consult current work programmes before preparing proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with programme structure (pillars, clusters, parts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Horizon Europe is structured into Pillar I (Excellent Science), Pillar II (Global Challenges and European Industrial Competitiveness) with clusters (Health; Culture, Creativity and Inclusive Society; Civil Security for Society; Digital, Industry and Space; Climate, Energy and Mobility; Food, Bioeconomy, Natural Resources, Agriculture and Environment), Pillar III (Innovative Europe), plus parts for widening participation and ERA-strengthening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should align to the relevant pillar/cluster objectives and to the specific programme/part under which the call is published (e.g., ERC, MSCA, EIC, Research Infrastructures, Widening). Check which pillar/cluster the call belongs to and tailor objectives accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme exclusivity and scope for specific programmes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific programme implementing Horizon Europe and EIT: Exclusive focus on civil applications; Specific programme: European Defence Fund: Exclusive focus on defence research and development; Complementary programme: Euratom Research and Training Programme: Focus on nuclear fusion and fission research and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your proposal's topic and intended application (civil vs defence vs nuclear) match the explicit scope of the programme under which you apply. Defence-related research should use European Defence Fund channels; nuclear R&D should use Euratom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission-oriented approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Horizon Europe incorporates research and innovation missions to increase the effectiveness of funding by pursuing clearly defined targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five missions have been identified (Adaptation to Climate Change; Climate‑Neutral and Smart Cities; Cancer; Soil Deal for Europe; Restore our Ocean and Waters). Proposals that contribute measurably to mission targets should indicate alignment with the mission approach; consult mission documentation and case studies prepared by Commission-contracted experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: European partnerships requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Horizon Europe supports European partnerships in which the EU, national authorities and/or the private sector jointly commit to support the development and implementation of a programme of research and innovation activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnerships should contribute to EU priorities, address complex challenges outlined in Horizon Europe and strengthen the European Research Area (ERA). Review partnership types and theme groupings (Health; Climate, energy and mobility; Culture, creativity and inclusive society; Digital, industry and space; Food, bioeconomy, natural resources, agriculture and environment) and contact listed partnership contacts for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widening participation and strengthening the ERA
rubrics_metrics.description: Part: Widening participation and spreading excellence; Reforming and enhancing the European Research and Innovation system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls and activities under WIDERA aim to increase participation from lower-performing R&I regions and spread excellence across the ERA. Check WIDERA work programmes and widening calls for eligibility, expected impact, and specific measures to support participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme evaluation, impact assessment and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission evaluates and monitors its funding programmes to assess the progress towards achieving the programmes' objectives and build an evidence base to improve their implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect monitoring and reporting requirements if funded; consult the programme analysis and monitoring approach documents, general overviews, participation guides and the implementation strategy for details on indicators, evaluation cycles and required deliverables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for excellence, innovation and competitiveness (moonshot projects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Horizon Europe 2028–2034 proposal will allow to launch ‘moonshot' scientific-driven projects designed to position Europe as a global leader in strategic fields and drive progress in areas such as clean aviation, the space economy, and next-generation AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ambitious, large-scale proposals targeting transformational impact in strategic fields may be eligible under future framework design; monitor the 2028–2034 proposal, thematic priorities and related calls for specific eligibility, budget and consortium requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding scale and timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicative funding amount for Horizon Europe for the period 2021–2027 is EUR 93.5 billion; the Commission proposed a €175 billion budget for Horizon Europe 2028–2034.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of programme budgets and multiannual framework context when planning projects and matching expectations to typical call funding envelopes and co-financing rules described in work programmes and model grant agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant support and information events
rubrics_metrics.description: Info days give prospective applicants and other stakeholders the opportunity to get information and ask questions about the main funding instruments and processes of Horizon Europe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend relevant Horizon Europe info days (online/live streaming available) for cluster-specific and call-specific briefings. Use these events and the research enquiry service to clarify call scope, application steps and evaluation modalities before submitting.
